name: Dunlop Cry Baby Wah (catalogue 21000)
description: Dunlop Cry Baby GCB-95 circuit (the reference netlist 71000), delivered for catalogue unit 21000. Rev-F-and-later GCB-95 with the MPSA13 Darlington input buffer and the two-transistor Fasel wah core: R2 1 kOhm from the 9 V input onto the C4 220 uF / C11 100 nF rail, C9 10 nF and R16 2.2 MOhm / R13 1.8 MOhm into Q3, R15 68 kOhm and C1 10 nF into Q1 (MPSA18, R4 22 kOhm collector, R9 390 Ohm emitter), L1 500 mH Fasel with its 17.5 Ohm DCR in parallel with R5 33 kOhm down to the bias node (R6 470 kOhm, R3 82 kOhm, C3 4.7 uF), C5 10 nF from the resonant node to Q2's emitter, and the VR1 100 kOhm log rocker pot feeding C6 220 nF into Q2 (R18 1 kOhm collector, R8 10 kOhm emitter). Output from Q1's collector through C8 220 nF, unbuffered, as on the pedal.

sources.title: Catalogue unit 21000 'Dunlop Cry Baby Wah' aliases: only Pd (pedal position) has a part in the circuit (VR1). LBP/D (mode, dry mix) and the PMin/PMid/PMax, RMin/RMid/RMax, LMin/LMid/LMax tuning triplets are the legacy behavioural wah model's parameters: a GCB-95 has no mode switch, no dry blend and no sweep/level tuning, so they are legacyOnly

ElectroSmash, 'Dunlop Cry Baby GCB-95 Circuit Analysis': schematic, BOM (Q0 MPSA13, Q1/Q2 MPSA18; Cin1 0.01 µF, Cin2 22 pF, C1 0.01 µF, C2 0.01 µF, C3 4.7 µF, C4/C5 0.22 µF, C6 220 µF, C7 0.1 µF; L1 500 mH; Rin1 2.2 MΩ, Rin2 1.8 MΩ, Rin3 1 kΩ, Rin4 10 kΩ; R1 68 kΩ, R2 1.5 kΩ, R3 22 kΩ, R4 390 Ω, R5/R6 470 kΩ, R7 33 kΩ, R8 82 kΩ, R9 1 kΩ, R10 10 kΩ; VR1 100 kΩ log), DC bias chart (8.6 V, 3 V, 4.9 V, 0.06 V, 0.6 V, 4.3 V), sweep 450 Hz-1.6 kHz with a 750 Hz peak at mid pot, up to 18 dB boost, inductor range 200 mH-1 H / 10-200 Ω
ElectroSmash archive mirror (MAS Effects) of the same article

B. W. K. McGrath, 'Crybaby GCB-95 schematic -- with correct component designators!' (2023): Dunlop board designators used here; the 1 kΩ (ElectroSmash 'Rin3') is the series dropping resistor in the 9 V line, not a collector resistor; R13 1.8 MΩ to the +9 V rail; C2/C7 not installed; R17 0 Ω jumper in series with L1

R. G. Keen, 'The Technology of Wah Pedals' (geofex.com): how the two-transistor wah works (Q2 + pot + Cf as a variable Miller capacitor), part roles (Rq sets Q, Cf sets the range, inductor 400-600 mH)
PedalPCB forum, 'Wah Inductors. No hype. Just measurements.': Dunlop red Fasel (toroid) 17.5 Ω / 565 mH (17 Ω / 583 mH); modern GCB-95 black-cylinder inductor 17.8 Ω / 599 mH

National Semiconductor MPSA18 SPICE card (IS 33.58f BF 236 BR 5.774 VAF 100 ISE 166.7f NE 1.579 CJE 7.547p CJC 4.948p), as distributed in the LTspice standard.bjt library (licence not stated; quoted as a factual parameter set)

MPSA18.note: National Semiconductor MPSA18 SPICE card (LTspice standard.bjt); IKF, RB/RE/RC, TF/TR and junction grading omitted. The card's BF 236 is below the datasheet hFE minimum (≈ 500 at 10 µA-10 mA, onsemi MPSA18); ElectroSmash's DC chart (Q2 base 4.3 V with 4.9 V on Q1's collector) implies hFE ≈ 290, consistent with this card

MPSA13_DIE.note: unverified: no MPSA13 card found. The MPSA13 Darlington is modelled as two dies with the MPSA18 card above (overall hFE ≈ 236² ≈ 55 000; datasheet MPSA13 hFE ≥ 5000 at 10 mA). Irrelevant to the sound as long as hFE is large: it is an emitter follower

controls.label: Wah (pedal position)
controls.note: VR1 100 kOhm log rocker pot (Dunlop 'Hot Potz' class): log end to ground, other end on the output (C8), wiper to Q2 via C6. 0 = heel down (maximum Miller multiplication, lowest resonance), 1 = toe down (highest resonance)

controls.label: Stereo
controls.note: Host stereo/mono routing flag; the pedal is mono. Stored only

controls.label: Mode
controls.note: Legacy behavioural wah 'mode' (low-band-pass blend). The GCB-95 has no mode switch or blend: the wah core is a single tuned resonant stage. Stored only

controls.label: Dry
controls.note: Legacy dry/wet mix. The pedal has no blend: the output is taken from the wah stage's collector through C8 220 nF. Stored only

controls.label: Freq Min
controls.note: Legacy behavioural sweep-limit parameter. The real sweep is set by VR1's track, C5 10 nF and the L1/C1 resonance; no part corresponds. Stored only

controls.label: Freq Mid
controls.note: Legacy behavioural sweep-shape parameter (log-taper midpoint). No part corresponds. Stored only

controls.label: Freq Max
controls.note: Legacy behavioural sweep-limit parameter. No part corresponds. Stored only

controls.label: Res Min
controls.note: Legacy behavioural Q parameter. The Q is fixed by R5 33 kOhm across the inductor and by the transistor stage; no control exists. Stored only

controls.label: Res Mid
controls.note: Legacy behavioural Q parameter. No part corresponds. Stored only

controls.label: Res Max
controls.note: Legacy behavioural Q parameter. No part corresponds. Stored only

controls.label: Level Min
controls.note: Legacy behavioural output-level trim per sweep region. The pedal has no level control. Stored only

controls.label: Level Mid
controls.note: Legacy behavioural output-level trim. No part corresponds. Stored only

controls.label: Level Max
controls.note: Legacy behavioural output-level trim. No part corresponds. Stored only

controls.label: On/Off
controls.note: The host's unit bypass. The netlist models the effect-on path. Stored only

parts.label: Supply dropping resistor
parts.note: Dunlop R2 (ElectroSmash 'Rin3', drawn there as Q0's collector resistor; McGrath 2023 traced it to the 9 V line). ElectroSmash's 8.6 V reading is this rail
ElectroSmash R4; the V847 has 510 Ω

parts.label: L1 Fasel 500 mH
parts.note: 500 mH per the schematics. Modern Dunlop red Fasel measures 565-583 mH (PedalPCB); Keen: 400-600 mH. Core loss and saturation are not modelled (see notes). R17 0 Ω jumper in series is merged

parts.label: L1 DC resistance
parts.note: unverified for any one pedal: Dunlop red Fasel measured 17.5 Ω (17 Ω on a second meter), modern GCB-95 stock inductor 17.8 Ω (PedalPCB). ElectroSmash only gives a 10-200 Ω acceptable range
ElectroSmash R8; the V847 has 100 kΩ

parts.label: Wah pot
parts.note: unverified: log end assumed on the ground lug (the usual wiring, giving a roughly log-spaced sweep); the exact Hot Potz taper is not published
